ex.t: 我们欢迎志愿者帮忙将回收材料改造成具有崭新而富有创意用途的物品。

ex.s: After we had twins and became a family of five, my husband and I decided to move from London back to Yorkshire, to be closer to my parents.
ex.t: 在有了双胞胎、成为一个五口之家后，我和丈夫决定从伦敦搬回约克郡，以便离我的父母更近。

ex.t: 我们把他们搬来和我们一起住，直到建造完成。

ex.t: 在老房子里的最后一个早晨，我们从令人头疼、没完没了的打包工作中歇下来，坐下来吃最后一顿早餐。

ex.t: 妈妈说出了我们所有人的想法：看到这个地方如此空荡荡，感觉很奇怪。

ex.t: 无论我们是否关注世界的“气味景观”，高温和污染都在使它发生变化。

ex.s: Even though we have other valuable things endangered by climate change, like food access, there is also an element of cultural identity, cultural survival, and history.
ex.t: 尽管我们还有其他因气候变化而受到威胁的宝贵事物，比如食物获取，但这里也有文化认同、文化存续和历史的元素。

ex.s: The 21st century has created a whole range of new types of professionals that we have never had before — or if not quite new, at least newly repackaged.
ex.t: 21世纪创造了一系列我们以前从未有过的新类型专业人士——或者即使不算全新，至少也是被重新包装过的。

ex.s: Similarly, the corporate world has certainly known its fair share of disruption, yet it is only in the last couple of decades that the “Disruptor” has become a recognisable figure in the way we talk about big business.
ex.t: 所有参与者都必须探讨通信或交通技术如何在整个历史中提升了美国人的生活质量。对许多人来说，技术意味着电脑、手持设备或飞往遥远行星的飞行器。然而，技术也是科学知识的应用，用以解决问题，以无数方式触动生活。

ex.s: When faced with such a fence, Chesterton thinks the fact that we can’t see the point of the fence is why we should not tear it down.
ex.t: 面对这样的栅栏，Chesterton认为，正因为我们看不出它的意义，才更不应该拆掉它。

ex.s: We could rephrase it like this: understand the wisdom in past decisions before you reject them.
ex.t: 但对"既有做法"不加批判的盲目遵从也可能使我们失去拥有更好日子的可能性。

ex.s: If we’re too impetuous, we can end up tearing out things we don’t yet realise we rely upon.
ex.t: 如果我们太鲁莽，最终可能会拆除那些我们尚未意识到自己正依赖着的东西。

ex.s: We need the ability to work out which messes are worth avoiding — because however impressively fast you move, some things can’t be easily unbroken.
ex.t: 我们需要具备分辨哪些混乱值得避免的能力——因为无论你行动得多快，有些东西一旦打破就很难复原。

ex.t: 从这篇文章关于Disruptor能推断出什么？

ex.t: 我们发现，那些被认为更有道德的人报告了更强的幸福感。

ex.s: When we fail at the right thing, persistence makes sense.
ex.t: 当我们在正确的事情上失败时，坚持是有意义的。

ex.s: We learn, adjust, and try again.
ex.t: 我们学习、调整，然后再试一次。

ex.s: But when we persist with the wrong thing, every bit of effort takes us further from where we are meant to be.
ex.t: 但当我们坚持做错误的事情时，每一点努力都让我们离本该所处的位置更远。

ex.s: By ending something, we create space for something new to grow.
ex.t: 通过结束某些事情，我们为新事物的成长创造了空间。

ex.s: We need to exit the things that don’t work anymore to be able to enter the ones that make sense for who we are today.
ex.t: 我们需要放弃那些不再有效的事情，才能进入那些对我们今天来说有意义的事物。

ex.s: We can imagine a different version of King Robert’s story.
ex.t: 我们可以想象罗伯特国王故事的另一个版本。

ex.s: “We need to speed up the development of green energy, and it will all get used,” says Wipke.
ex.t: Wipke说：“我们需要加快绿色能源的发展，而它都会被用上。”

ex.s: We invest a lot in roads that help us rush through, but we fail to account for the true costs.
ex.t: 我们投入巨资修建让我们匆匆穿行的道路，却忽略了真正的代价。

ex.s: Do we really recognise what it costs us as a society when children can’t move safely around our communities?
ex.t: 当孩子无法在我们的社区安全出行时，我们作为社会究竟意识到这让我们付出了什么代价吗？

ex.s: “We should be looking into upgrading drinking water treatment plants so they remove microplastics.”
ex.t: 我们应该考虑升级饮用水处理厂，以便去除微塑料。

ex.s: His reply came as a surprise — a shock, actually: “Not a chance.” Clearly, he was unhappy over the way we had parted.
ex.t: 他的回复令人意外——其实是震惊：“绝不可能。”显然，他对我们分开时的方式感到不快。

ex.s: From technological solutions to educational campaigns, food producers and sellers are looking for ways to use more of what we’re already growing.
ex.t: 从技术解决方案到教育活动，食品生产者和销售者正在寻找方法来更多地利用我们已经种植的东西。

ex.t: 关于wastED我们能了解到什么？

ex.t: 成熟的矩阵花园不需要我们给大多数花园提供的那种生命支持：肥料、分株和定期浇水。

ex.s: To reduce our impact, we can take simple steps: empty the fridge before heading out, and choose sustainable dining options.
ex.t: 为了减少我们的影响，我们可以采取简单的步骤：出门前清空冰箱，并选择可持续的就餐选择。

ex.s: What can we learn from this passage?
ex.t: 从这篇文章中我们可以学到什么？

ex.s: In my defence, I did what we’ve all done before, which is to repeat received wisdom without exploring the nuances.
ex.t: 为我自己辩护一下，我做了我们所有人都做过的事，那就是在不探究细节的情况下重复人云亦云的观点。

ex.s: Science provides a guide we can use to harness the way we perform these comparisons to reduce their negative emotional impacts.
ex.t: 科学提供了一个指南，我们可以借此引导自己进行这些比较的方式，以减少其负面情绪影响。

ex.s: How we feel about ourselves rests not just on whom we compare ourselves with but also on how we think about that comparison.
ex.t: 我们如何看自己，不仅取决于我们和谁比较，也取决于我们如何看待那种比较。

ex.s: That’s something we all have control over.
ex.t: 这是我们所有人都能控制的。

ex.s: Considering the stories we tell about ourselves can help us to change our minds for better.
ex.t: 思考我们讲述的关于自己的故事，有助于我们改善自己的想法。

ex.s: Then, in the 1980s, Bob Johnson created the life story model of identity, in which he proposes that, as we go through life, these core features are built in with our memories to create a personal story through which we understand our lives.
ex.t: 之后,在1980年代,鲍勃·约翰逊创立了身份的人生故事模型,他在模型中提出,在我们经历生命时,这些核心特征与我们的记忆一起构建,以创造一个个人故事,我们通过这个故事来理解我们的生活.

ex.s: Our life story is something that starts coming together in our teenage years, when we begin to organise our lives into chapters around key events or life changes, and begin to see ourselves as both the central character and, to a varying extent, the story’s author.
ex.t: 我们的人生故事在青少年时期开始成形，那时我们开始把生活围绕关键事件或人生变化整理成一个个章节，并开始把自己视为故事的中心人物，并且在不同程度上也视为这个故事的创作者。

ex.s: The good news is that there is evidence we can learn to change our own story.
ex.t: 好消息是，有证据表明我们可以学会改写自己的人生故事。

ex.t: 从这篇文章中我们可以学到什么？

ex.t: 无论晴雨我们都会照常工作。

ex.t: 面对这些不完美的生物多样性数据集，我们能做些什么？

ex.t: 关于现在收集到的物种记录，我们知道什么？

ex.t: 所以我绝对相信，仅因为短篇故事我们就会迎来更多乘客，”她说。

ex.t: 我们热衷于减少环境中的废弃物、碳排放和化学品，”一位BMF员工说。

ex.s: Given the astonishing potential of AI to transform our lives, we all need to take action to deal with our AI-powered future, and this is where AI by Design: A Plan for Living with Artificial Intelligence comes in.
ex.t: 鉴于AI改变我们生活的惊人潜力，我们都需要采取行动来应对这个由AI驱动的未来，而这正是《AI by Design：与人工智能共处之计》一书的用武之地。

ex.s: She says it is essential that we keep control of artificial intelligence, or risk being sidelined and perhaps even worse.
ex.t: 她说，我们必须始终掌控人工智能，否则就有被边缘化甚至更糟的风险。

ex.s: She explains we are at a “tipping point” in history and must act now to prevent an extinction-level event for humanity.
ex.t: 她解释说，我们正处于历史上的一个“临界点”，必须立刻行动，以防人类遭遇灭绝级事件。

ex.s: We need to consider how we want our future with AI to pan out.
ex.t: 我们需要思考希望我们与人工智能的未来如何展开。

ex.t: 以下是一些建议，帮助你做出明智的决定，减轻我们游览之地的压力，并提升我们的体验。

ex.t: 那么，我们应该停止旅行吗？

ex.s: As adults we face a version of the marshmallow test every day.
ex.t: 成功之母是勤奋。

ex.s: We are tempted by sugary treats because our ancestors lived in a calorie-poor world, and our brains developed a response mechanism to these treats that reflected their value — a feeling of reward and satisfaction.
ex.t: 我们会被含糖零食诱惑，因为我们的祖先生活在热量匮乏的世界里，而我们的大脑形成了一种对这些零食的响应机制，反映出它们的价值——一种奖励和满足感。

ex.s: But as we’ve reshaped the world around us, dramatically reducing the cost and effort involved in obtaining calories, we still have the same brains we had thousands of years ago, and this mismatch is at the heart of why so many of us struggle to resist tempting foods that we know we shouldn’t eat.
ex.t: 但当我们重新塑造周围的世界,大幅降低获取卡路里所需的成本和努力时,我们仍然有我们几千年前拥有的同样的大脑,这种不匹配现象正是我们许多人努力抵制诱人的食物的核心,而我们知道我们不应该吃这些食物。

ex.s: Therefore, just as we need to be more thoughtful about our caloric consumption, we also need to be more thoughtful about our information consumption, resisting the temptation of the mental “junk food” in order to manage our time most effectively.
ex.t: 因此，正如我们需要更审慎地对待热量摄入，我们也需要更审慎地对待信息摄入，抵制精神“垃圾食品”的诱惑，以最有效地管理时间。
